sasha_ml: Heads-up — trying to bring up hf repo 'gpt-mini-chat-v2' with hf2redwood. The repo has a tokenizer.json (fast) but no tokenizer_config.json. hf2redwood logs show it falling back to slow tokenizer and chat templates are mis-parsed. Anyone seen this pattern?

jordan: yup, seen that before. fast tokenizer metadata can live in tokenizers.json or tokenizer.json depending on tokenizer lib version. conversion script expects tokenizer_config.json for some fields (like bos_token, eos_token, and pad). If missing, we end up with inconsistent special tokens.

sasha_ml: exact log: `WARN: no tokenizer_config.json found, attempting heuristic mapping from tokenizer.json` then `ERROR: fast tokenizer missing backend file, fallback to slow` — fallback increases inference latency ~2-3x in our microbenchmarks.

liam: can you paste the tokenizer.json minimal snippet? sometimes `added_tokens` is present but named differently.

sasha_ml: here — pasted output from the repo:
```json
{"model_max_length": 2048, "special_tokens_map": {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>"}, "vocab_size": 50257}
```

liam: ok that `special_tokens_map` isn't the standard `tokenizer_config.json` layout, hf2redwood parser didn't pick it up. Also check for `tokenizer.json` vs `tokenizers.json` (note plural) — transformers/tokenizers changed formats.

qa_ops: we noticed quality regressions in quantization runs yesterday on that model. When the fast tokenizer isn't loaded native, tokenization differs slightly and quantized model prompts get shifted resulting in larger degredation on rouge/accuracy tests. Could explain the regression spike.

sasha_ml: here's the conversion command we ran:
```
./hf2redwood --model-path ./gpt-mini-chat-v2 --output ./redwood-ready --quantize 4bit --preserve-config
```

deploy-bot: conversion job 2026-03-17-22-34 started (id: cj-8421). Status: failed -> partial (fallback slow tokenizer).

jordan: quick hack: add a tokenizer_config.json with the fields the converter expects (bos_token, eos_token, pad_token, model_max_length). converter will pick it up and create a fast tokenizer if the tokenizers backend files are present. But if the repo lacks the tokenizers lib serialized backend (the .json for tokenizers library), you still may not get the Rust fast tokenizer.

liam: alternative is to extend hf2redwood to be more tolerant: map `special_tokens_map` -> tokenizer_config.json fields and check for `tokenizers.json`/`tokenizer.json` variants. Also verify `added_tokens` vs `added_special_tokens`. I'll draft a small patch.

sasha_ml: can we also add a unit test that simulates missing tokenizer_config.json but present tokenizer.json with different key names? Regression came up only during quantization A/B tests.

qa_ops: agree, add an eval that runs a baseline prompt set (20 prompts) and compares tokenization hashes and top-1 generation diffs pre/post conversion. That's how we detected the silent drift.

liam: quick diff idea: if fast tokenizer backend missing, assert that slow tokenizer output token ids == expected ids from huggingface Python tokenizers for a sample set. If mismatch, fail conversion.

jordan: FYI there's an edge: chat templates in model repo referenced `system_prompt` in a `chat_config.json` which our converter expected under `tokenizer_config.json['chat']`. Without that, we map wrong role names and end up with malformed prompt blocks. So this is two related mismatches: tokenizer metadata and chat template placement.

sasha_ml: noted. I'll open a single PR that: 1) heuristically maps known variants from tokenizer.json/tokenizers.json -> tokenizer_config.json, 2) validates presence of fast tokenizer backend and falls back with clear metrics, 3) adds chat template mapping from chat_config.json if present, and 4) adds test cases + a guard for quantization-eval drift.

liam: thanks. tag me on the PR. Also add a short changelog entry for conversion behavior so partners know fallback will affect latency and may change outputs.

deploy-bot: conversion job cj-8421 updated: partial -> pending-fix.

sasha_ml: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hf2redwood/pull/644 — includes mapping and tests. Requesting review from @liam @jordan. Steps: patch -> run conversion job -> run quant-eval -> flip to dedicated test infra.

jordan: ack. I'll run the conversion locally and push a small sample artifact so QA can re-run the quantization experiments.

qa_ops: once we have the artifact, we'll re-run the 4-bit sweep and post the delta table in #model-evals. For now, marking the regression as 'under investigation'. :mag:
